root_cause_criterion.missing_conjunct: the message-separator search over `buffer` is length-bounded by `buffer_end - buffer`
root_cause_criterion.criterion:
At the message-separator search site, the parser must search the remaining span `[buffer, buffer_end)` with a length-bounded primitive instead of calling `strstr(buffer, "

")` on an unterminated byte span. The vulnerable code's only preceding checks are `buffer < buffer_end` and `*buffer != '
'`, which still admit the one-byte suffix left by `git_signature__parse`.
root_cause_criterion.description: In the staged witness, only the final trailing space byte remains when `tag_parse` reaches line 142. The vulnerable original still calls unbounded `strstr`, so the protected separator-search event executes with no span bound and ASan reports a 2-byte read crossing the heap allocation. The fixed original replaces that call with `git__memmem(buffer, buffer_end - buffer, "\n\n", 2)`, satisfying the missing bounded-search obligation while exercising the same search site.

nodes.state: At the separator-search call, `buffer + 1 == buffer_end`, so the search begins on the last in-bounds byte of the heap-backed input.
When `git_signature__parse` returns after consuming `tagger <>\n`, `buffer` points at the witness's lone trailing space byte and `buffer + 1 == buffer_end`.

edges.relation: The same `buffer` pointer returned by `git_signature__parse` reaches the later separator search unchanged; no code between the two sites advances or rewrites `buffer` before the search call.
